sections.h2: What kind of housing market is Coconut Creek in Broward County?
sections.html: Coconut Creek is a Broward County city of 58,626 residents in the July 2025 Census estimate, up from 52,909 in 2010 and 57,833 in 2020. It is compact, with 11.17 square miles of land and about 5,179 people per square mile in 2020. Check whether your home belongs to a homeowner or condominium association, since the vacation rental affidavit on the city's site refers to notice to a mandatory association and its rules can add steps to a sale.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Coconut Creek homes?
sections.html:
The Census reports a median owner-occupied value of $309,600 for 2020 to 2024, with 64.8% of housing owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $2,102 a month, so owners of rental units can compare that income with what a sale would bring.

  • Households: 24,304, with 2.39 people each.
  • Monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $2,162; without one: $890.
  • Foreign-born residents: 33.0%; language other than English at home: 39.6%.
  • Residents 65 or older: 20.1%; under 18: 21.8%.
  • Mean commute: 29.6 minutes.

About 39.6% of residents speak a language other than English at home, so read every contract and disclosure fully, and ask for a translation if you need one.

sections.h2: Does Coconut Creek allow vacation rentals, and does that matter for a sale?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's vacation rental page says its regulations do not prohibit vacation rentals or limit how long or how often a home is rented. They exist to protect neighborhoods and life safety, and every vacation rental must register and obtain a Vacation Rental Certification.

If you hold one, tell buyers up front. A certification is part of the property's income story, and a buyer who wants it must apply on their own. The city lists these details:

  • Application or registration fee: $250. Renewal: $250. Re-inspection: $40.
  • Registrations expire annually and must be renewed before September 30.
  • Fire safety and code compliance inspections come before the first certificate, under Ordinance No. 2021-003, by appointment.
  • Packet items: a Florida DBPR transient public lodging license, Florida Department of Revenue sales tax registration, a Broward County business tax receipt and Broward tourist development tax registration.

The city page also gives a notarized-letter option for owners whose booking sites collect taxes. Ask the city's business tax office for the current form.

sections.h2: What should a Coconut Creek landlord do before selling a rented house?
sections.html:
Read the lease first. A month-to-month tenancy takes at least 30 days of notice under Florida law, and a tenant who fails to pay rent receives 3 days of written notice, not counting weekends and court holidays. Florida's eviction statute lays out the notice and the court steps, so follow them if a tenant must leave before closing.

A buyer who takes the tenant as is keeps the rent flowing and avoids a turnover period. Put the lease, security deposit amount and rent ledger in the contract package.

sections.h2: How is documentary stamp tax handled on a Broward deed?
sections.html:
Broward uses the standard Florida rate of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration. Miami-Dade is the only county with a different rate. Everyone named on the deed is liable to the state for the tax, whichever side agrees in the contract to pay it, and the Broward clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.

Clerks also charge recording fees set by statute: $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus other per-page charges. Ask the closing agent for the line items so you see what is on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: How do Broward homestead and property tax dates affect a Coconut Creek sale?
sections.html:
Florida assesses every parcel on January 1, and a homestead exemption of up to $50,000 requires an application by March 1 with proof that the home was your permanent residence by January 1. The first $25,000 applies to all taxes, and the second $25,000 applies to value above $50,000 and only to non-school taxes.

Save Our Homes limits annual assessed value growth to the lower of 3 percent or inflation. A sale is a change of ownership that resets the property to just value the next January 1. Bills arrive in November, discounts step down from 4 percent to 1 percent through February, and unpaid taxes are delinquent on April 1. If you sell mid-year, the title company prorates the tax at closing.

sections.h2: What if a Coconut Creek owner faces foreclosure or an inherited house?
sections.html:
Foreclosure is a court process, and the clerk holds the sale 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the lender agrees to a longer period. Selling before that date leaves the lender paid from the proceeds. For an inherited home, summary administration may fit an estate under $150,000 or a death more than two years back, and creditors must file claims within the statutory window.

Both situations reward early calls to the servicer, a Florida attorney or the probate clerk. A cash buyer can close around those dates, but the court's timetable controls.

sections.h2: What if property taxes on a Coconut Creek house go unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1, and the Broward tax collector sells tax certificates on unpaid items by June 1. The buyer of a certificate bids the interest rate down in quarter-percent steps, and the lowest rate wins. The holder cannot contact the owner for payment until two years after April 1 of the issue year.

After two years the holder can apply for a tax deed, which carries a $75 application fee, and the clerk runs the auction. Homestead property has a higher opening bid that includes half the assessed value. A seller with delinquent taxes can pay them from sale proceeds at closing, so ask the title company for a payoff figure.

sections.h2: Which Florida tax breaks might apply to a Coconut Creek owner?
sections.html:
Owners 65 or older may qualify for an additional homestead exemption of up to $50,000 if a city or county ordinance allows it and household income is within the limit. A disabled ex-servicemember with a 10 percent or greater rating, honorably discharged and a Florida resident, gets a $5,000 reduction in assessed value. Total and permanent service-connected disability may qualify for a full homestead exemption. With 1,850 veterans in the city, according to the Census, these matter to a real group of Coconut Creek owners.

Homestead ends when you rent the home or stop living in it. A servicemember may rent out a homestead without losing it. Ask the Broward property appraiser which exemptions are on your parcel before you close.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Coconut Creek house that has a vacation rental certification?
faqs.a: Yes. The certification is held by the owner, and a buyer who wants to keep renting short term must register on their own. Check the city's annual September 30 renewal date and your fee status before closing.

faqs.q: Do I owe the city anything before I sell my Coconut Creek home?
faqs.a: Ask the city's Building Division to check for open permits and the code office for open violations, since either can hold up closing.

faqs.q: How fast can a cash sale close in Coconut Creek?
faqs.a: Often within a few weeks, because no lender or appraisal is needed. HOA approval, title work and any lien payoffs can still add days.

faqs.q: Who pays the Broward doc stamp tax?
faqs.a: The state makes every party to the deed liable, and contracts usually assign payment to the seller. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration.

faqs.q: What happens to my Coconut Creek tenant if the house sells?
faqs.a: The lease generally continues unless it ends or proper notice is given. A month-to-month tenant gets at least 30 days of notice under Florida law.
